title: `round`, `floor`, `ceil`, `arctan2`, `sqrt` and `pow` on Float32 and Float64: zero signs, types and `pow(1, ±inf)`
verdict: as the profile: `round_zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `pow_one_inf` = `ONE`; no integer conversion (`float_to_int` does not arise)
description: `round(0)`, `ceil` and `floor` keep the column's type (Float32 stays Float32, Float64 Float64) and never return an integer: `float_to_int` does not arise for them (`round(1e30)` stays 1e30). A negative value that reaches zero gives `-0.0` (`round(-0.4)`, `ceil(-0.4)`, `ceil(-0.6)`), and `-0.0` stays `-0.0` through all three, on both widths. NaN and ±inf come back unchanged.

`pl.arctan2` and `sqrt` keep the sign of a zero argument: `arctan2(-0.0, 1)` and `sqrt(-0.0)` are `-0.0`, `arctan2(0.0, -1)` is π and `arctan2(±0.0, -0.0)` is -π, in the column's own width (Float32 π is 3.141592502593994).
`pow(1, ±inf)`, `pow(-1, ±inf)`, `pow(1, NaN)` and `pow(NaN, 0)` are 1.0 on Float32 as on Float64 (polars-pow-one-inf).
reference: `round_zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `pow_one_inf` = `ONE` (D40). `round`, `floor` and `ceil` return the float, so `float_to_int` does not arise.
